The thin-envelope decoupling is real: git diff of policy_check.py/two_key.py/decision.py is EMPTY, and the readers were verified by reading (not just the selftest) to be purely .get()-based with no strict-schema/unknown-field rejection - and the gate's own check_json uses a subset check, so a back-ref'd approval/verdict passes the GATE too, not just the readers. findings.text: Finding #1 (forward-looking, address): request_hash is required-present but the CHEAP in-memory self-consistency invariant request_hash == request_digest(record) is NOT enforced at W2 (only the expensive repo-recompute is rightly deferred to W5). Because the build order is W2->W6->W3->W4->W5-logic, W3 (projection) and W4 (doorbell) ship BEFORE W5 enforces it, so the material-change baseline is unvalidated at creation. Fix: enforce the 2-line self-consistency check at W2 (this spec's follow-up), so no intermediate consumer trusts an unverified request_hash. (W3 already mitigates by displaying bound_artifact.digest, but that is not guaranteed by W2.)

Finding #2 (observation): decision_choice tier derivation is opportunistic - _check_decision_choice_tier stands down when bound_artifact.ref does not resolve to a file or the decision declares no risk. So an accepted decision_choice with an unresolvable ref can carry a tier inconsistent with its decision while passing (acceptance is still bound by digest + settlement.path). W6 (authz reads the tier) must not assume W2 universally guarantees tier == decision.risk.
Finding #3 (benign, review-lane): validate_record is a single ~41-complexity function, consistent with decision.py/check_plan norms; worth splitting eventually, not now.
